326097.title: The reduced tangent-cone conjecture for K-orbit closures
326097.statement:
Let $p\in Y_{\gamma}$ be a point of the $K$-orbit closure, and let $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m_p}\mathcal O_{p,Y_{\gamma}}$ be the associated graded local ring. **Reduced tangent-cone conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m_p}\mathcal O_{p,Y_{\gamma}})
$$

is reduced. This was checked exhaustively for all cases with $p+q\leq 7$, but remains open in general.

326377.title: Equality between gem-complexity and Matveev complexity for lens spaces
326377.statement:
Let $L(p,q)$ be a lens space, let $k(L(p,q))$ denote its gem-complexity, and let $c(L(p,q))$ denote its Matveev complexity.

**Lens-space complexity equality conjecture.** For every $p\ge 3$,

$$
k(L(p,q))=5+2\cdot c(L(p,q)).
$$

The claim is suggested by propositions in the paper and by equality in specified infinite classes; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

327574.title: Conjecture on Theorem 2 for Artinian lex-ideals
327574.statement: Let $L$ be an Artinian lex-ideal in the polynomial ring $\mathbf{k}[x,y,z]$. The Boij–Söderberg decomposition of $L$ is the decomposition into pure diagrams described by Theorem 2. **The conjecture.** The statement of Theorem 2 holds for all Artinian lex-ideals in $\mathbf{k}[x,y,z]$. The claim extends the preceding result to the remaining cases and is stated without a proof in the supplied text.

327993.title: The algorithmic orientation-reversing symmetry problem for irreducible 3-manifolds
327993.statement: Let $M$ be a closed, orientable, irreducible $3$-manifold. **Algorithmic orientation-reversing symmetry conjecture.** There is an algorithm that determines whether $M$ admits an orientation-reversing self-homeomorphism. This problem is the remaining obstruction identified in the paper to deciding homeomorphism for all closed, orientable $3$-manifolds; the source does not state a resolution.

328316.title: The equality case for the improved positive-writhe inequality
328316.statement: Let the assumptions of Lemma~(c) hold, and consider the inequality in Remark~. **Equality conjecture.** Under these assumptions, the inequality is an equality. This proposed equality would provide the formula for $w_\tau(\zeta_2)$ needed to rule out more generally sequences of cylinders converging to buildings as in case (iii) of Proposition~(c) with arbitrary $d_2$.

328509.title: Cyclic Sylow lifting conjecture
328509.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group with a cyclic $p$-Sylow subgroup, and let $k[[z]]/k[[t]]$ be a $G$-extension. **Cyclic Sylow lifting conjecture.** For every such extension, the KGB obstruction is the only obstruction to lifting. The paper places this among open problems concerning local Oort groups and lifting of local extensions.

328683.title: Cyclic monodromy conjecture for Bethe vectors
328683.statement: Let $\fg$ be the Lie algebra in the Gaudin model, and let the theorem referred to in the source as Theorem~ assert the cyclic monodromy property for the associated Bethe vectors. **Cyclic monodromy conjecture.** Theorem~ holds for arbitrary $\fg$. The surrounding section identifies this as a variant of the Bethe Ansatz conjecture, but the supplied context does not state the theorem's content.

329002.title: Class-number-one conjecture for the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_5$-extension
329002.statement: Let $\mathbb{B}_{5,n}$ denote the $n$th layer of the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_5$-extension of $\mathbb{Q}$. **$\mathbb{Z}_5$-extension class-number conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$, the class number of $\mathbb{B}_{5,n}$ is $1$. This is a special case of the main conjecture, and the paper estimates its likelihood using Cohen–Lenstra heuristics. It remains open.

329103.title: Existence conjecture for genus-detecting higher-order Alexander torsion
329103.statement:
Let $K$ be a knot. **Genus-detecting higher-order torsion conjecture.** There exists an epimorphism $\gamma\colon\pi_K\to\Gamma$ onto a torsion-free elementary-amenable group such that

$$
\deg\bigl(\tau(K,\gamma)\bigr)=2\operatorname{genus}(K)-1.
$$

This would provide a higher-order Alexander torsion attaining the sharp genus bound for every knot. The source gives no resolution.

330110.title: Fundamental-set conjecture for odd integers in the Collatz system
330110.statement: Let $d_i$ denote the values used in the proposed Collatz-based number system, and let the odd integers be the odd members of the system. **Fundamental-set conjecture.** The values $d_i$ are the fundamental, or principal, sets for all odd integers, because they solely represent the sets from which every odd number could be derived. The source gives no further proof or resolution of this assertion.

330534.title: Greenberg's conjecture on cyclotomic Iwasawa modules
330534.statement: For the cyclotomic Iwasawa module $X$, let $X^+$ and $X^-$ be the eigenspaces for complex conjugation. **Greenberg's conjecture.** For every $N$, $X^+$ has finite cardinality. In particular, $X^-$ is pseudocyclic. This conjecture is used in the paper to explain why the localization hypothesis in its Gorenstein theorem is expected to be weak; no general proof is supplied.

330606.title: Braun–Solus stable hypersimplex h-star unimodality conjecture
330606.statement: For positive integers $n$ and $r$, let $\Delta_{n,2}^{\operatorname{stab}(r)}$ denote the $r$-stable hypersimplex. **Braun–Solus' conjecture.** The $h^*$-vector of $\Delta_{n,2}^{\operatorname{stab}(r)}$ is unimodal for all $r$. The source records this as an open question; unimodality is known for $r=2$, $r=3$, and $r=\lfloor n/2\rfloor-1$.

330976.title: Chi-map isomorphism conjecture for wreath product algebras
330976.statement: For each $m\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\chi_m$ denote the algebra map defined in the paper. **Chi-map isomorphism conjecture.** The map $\chi_m$ is an isomorphism of algebras for all $m\in\mathbb{N}$. This is a generalization of the corresponding result known when $B=\mathbb{F}$; the source also identifies it with a conjecture of Cautis and Licata in their special case.

331362.title: Hilbert-space Erdős discrepancy conjecture
331362.statement:
Let $x_1,x_2,\dots$ be a sequence of unit vectors in a real or complex Hilbert space. **Hilbert-space Erdős discrepancy conjecture.** For every $C$ there exist $n$ and $d$ such that

$$
\left\|\sum_{m=1}^n x_{md}\right\|\geq C.
$$

Since $\mathbb{R}$ is a Hilbert space, this generalizes Erdős's discrepancy conjecture. The source explicitly states that this conjecture is open.

331657.title: The uniruledness conjecture for compact Kähler manifolds
331657.statement:
Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold.

**Uniruledness conjecture.** $X$ is uniruled, meaning covered by rational curves, if and only if

$$
H^0(X,K_X^{\otimes k})=\{0\}
$$

for all $k>0$.

This is presented as a consequence of the Abundance Conjecture and gives a pluricanonical criterion for uniruledness in the compact Kähler setting.

331705.title: Starlikeness conjecture for Cassinian balls in starlike domains
331705.statement: Let $G\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a domain that is starlike with respect to $x\in G$, and let $B_{c_G}(x,r)$ denote the Cassinian ball of radius $r$. **Starlikeness conjecture.** For every $r>0$, the ball $B_{c_G}(x,r)$ is starlike with respect to $x$. This is a proposed extension of convexity results to starlike domains, and the paper does not establish it.

332276.title: The weighted higher-order discrepancy lower-bound conjecture
332276.statement:
Let $D_r^w(m,d)_\infty$ denote the minimal weighted $r$-discrepancy in dimension $d$, where $m$ is the number of nodes. **Weighted higher-order discrepancy lower-bound conjecture.** For all $d,r\in\mathbb N$,

$$
D_r^w(m,d)_\infty \ge C(r,d)m^{-r}(\log m)^{d-1}.
$$

This generalizes the conjectured lower bound for the classical star-discrepancy; the source presents it as an open problem.

332527.title: The nilpotent-group conjecture for the sum of element orders
332527.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite nilpotent group, and let $S(G)$ denote the sum of the orders of all elements of $G$.

**Nilpotent-group conjecture.** One has

$$
S(G)\geq |G|,
$$

and equality holds if and only if $G$ is cyclic.

This extends the preceding results for non-abelian $p$-groups with cyclic maximal subgroups. The supplied text gives no resolution of the conjecture for all finite nilpotent groups.

332535.title: The ellipsoid conjecture for cylindrical covering parameters
332535.statement:
Let $\mathbf{K}$ be an ellipsoid in $\mathbb{E}^d$, and let $\operatorname{cyl}_k(\mathbf{K})$ denote its $k$-th cylindrical covering parameter. **Ellipsoid conjecture.** For every $2<k<d$,

$$
\operatorname{cyl}_k(\mathbf{K})=1.
$$

The equality is known for $k=1$ and $k=2$; the paper presents the assertion for all remaining $k$ as an open conjecture.

333757.title: The conjecture that all finite-index subgroups of Thompson group F are 2-generated
333757.statement: Let $F$ denote Thompson group $F$, and let a group be **2-generated** if it has a generating set with two elements. **The finite-index generation conjecture.** Every finite-index subgroup of $F$ is $2$-generated. Finite-index subgroups of $F$ can have generating sets of this size in known examples, but the assertion for all finite-index subgroups is presented as a conjecture and remains open.
